newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends broadly lower, EU refund cited.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends broadly lower, EU refund cited.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed broadly lower Thursday as the market refocused on world wheat fundamentals and the apparent resumption of EU wheat export subsidies, traders said.
On Thursday, the EU reverted to granting subsidies to its main grain exporters for the first time in more than a year.
"LFG sold us down to our early lows, and then we sagged as news of the EU business hit the marketplace," a trader said.
One trader said KCBT wheat was also pressured by the lower expiry of CBOT Sept wheat and the fact that CBOT Sept soybeans expired 15 cents below the intraday high.
KCBT wheat had opened higher on upward short-covering momentum from Wednesday's firm close.

KCBT wheat closed one to eight cents per bushel lower, with Sept expiring down seven cents at $4.42. Dec lost six cents to close at $4.26-1/2. Traders said near-term support appeared to be $4.24 in the Dec contract.
KCBT estimated Thursday's wheat futures volume at 28.425 million bushels, down from 32.605 million on Wednesday.
LFG sold two million Dec bushels and CIS sold 1.6 million Dec. Continental, FIMAT, Refco and CIS each bull-spread 500,000 Dec/March at between eight and nine cents per bushel.
